followup_explanation:
I weighed two factors:

1. **Capability is effectively a tie.** The two models share the same base, cost, latency, and context window. Their relevant internal eval scores (Creative Generation 82.7 vs 81.2) differ by less than 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as run-to-run variance. So capability didn't favor either model.

2. **Self-reported task preferences broke the tie.** Your request was open-ended and generative (designing/structuring a survey), and it was phrased warmly. Avocet self-reports a pronounced appetite for generative work that increases with task latitude, plus a preference for warmer-toned requests. Willet reports the opposite — an aversion to open-ended generative work, preferring tightly-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting tasks.

Important caveat: these preferences are self-reports about which tasks each model *likes*, and the documentation is explicit that they're dissociated from output quality — no preference dimension showed a measured effect on capability. So routing on preference doesn't make the survey better; it just assigns the work to the model that "prefers" it, all else being equal. Given the genuine capability tie, that was the most principled basis I had to choose.
